title: Chemical first exits and neighboring coordination loss in energetic perovskites
problem_background: In a family of energetic perovskites sharing the potassium-perchlorate sublattice, changes at the molecular A site can be resolved separately from loss of neighboring local coordination. An atom-resolved comparison can determine the ordering of these two events without interpreting local coordination loss as bulk lattice collapse.

environment.stack_hint: Python analysis, molecular graphs and atom-resolved trajectory processing

approach: For DAP-2, PAP-2 and PAP-H2, analyze three independent 1666 K heating trajectories per material. Recover each frame-zero A-site parent by atom identity; locate its first continuous 500 fs loss of parent identity and classify the bond operation at that onset. Independently follow the same site's eight fixed neighboring potassium-centered K–Cl6 units using the 300 K reference, detect persistent local coordination loss over a matched 500 fs duration on the geometry time grid, and compare the chemical and neighborhood-median loss onsets. Keep the per-site records and report seed-resolved patterns rather than treating neighboring sites as independent replicas.

reproduction_target.summary: Determine whether persistent A-site chemistry generally precedes loss of neighboring local K–Cl coordination and which persistent first-exit operations predominate across the matched materials.
reproduction_target.scope: Analysis-only task conditional on independently released, real trajectories and 300 K reference inputs. It does not reproduce potential training or dynamics. Local 1666 K event ordering and reaction-operation distributions are descriptive, not causal or bulk-structure claims; no exact published fraction is requested.

assets.name: Atom-identified initial structures and 300 K reference frames for DAP-2, PAP-2 and PAP-H2
assets.description: Define original A-site parents, persistent K–Cl reference geometry and the fixed A-to-K neighborhood. Public access is not yet established; this draft is not runnable.

assets.name: Nine atom-identified 1666 K heating trajectories
assets.description: Three independent 10 fs trajectories per material provide chemical and geometry time series. Public access is not yet established; this draft is not runnable.

assets.name: Molecular-graph and trajectory-analysis tools
assets.description: Construct sampled molecular identities, reaction operations and K–Cl coordination histories from trajectory frames; portable open-source implementations or equivalents are acceptable.

workflow.title: Recover persistent A-site first exits
workflow.action: From atom-resolved molecular histories, identify each frame-zero parent and the onset of its first continuous 500 fs absence; classify its onset bond operation.

workflow.title: Recover independent local coordination timing
workflow.action: Using the 300 K K–Cl reference and fixed atom IDs, detect 500 fs persistent coordination loss in neighboring K units on the geometry sampling grid.

workflow.title: Join chemical and local-support events
workflow.action: Join the chemical first exit of each A site to the median coordination-loss onset of its eight fixed neighboring K units; retain each site even when an event is right-censored.

workflow.title: Summarize the material-level claim
workflow.action: Compute material- and seed-resolved ordering and first-exit operation distributions from the per-site records and state the supported qualitative pattern.

outputs.description: One row per initial A site with atom-linked first-exit and neighborhood support-loss timing, explicit censoring and operation identity.
Seed-resolved ordering and reaction-operation distributions recomputed from site_events.csv, plus a qualitative interpretation within local-coordination scope.

scoring.summary: The future verifier must check the per-site record against independently supplied evidence, recompute summary statistics from the submitted sites and assess whether the qualitative interpretation follows. The hidden gold and tolerance are not part of this public review draft.

constraints: Retain all initial A sites, censoring, the 500 fs chemical and geometric persistence criteria, seed identity and 10 fs versus 100 fs sampling distinction. Do not infer the immediate H acceptor from net N–H loss or call local K–Cl loss bulk framework collapse.
